ai.description: The Chengalam caecilian reaches 20–25 cm. It is dark brown with a paler venter and features a distinctively pointed snout and interrupted primary annuli. It lacks a tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus interruptus* is uniquely distinguished by its incomplete primary annuli, which fail to encircle the body ventrally, unlike all other Indian caecilians.
ai.habitat: The Chengalam caecilian inhabits moist, shaded soil within evergreen forest patches and rubber plantations in the Western Ghats at elevations between 200 and 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Chengalam caecilian is primarily nocturnal, emerging from its subterranean burrows at night to forage for earthworms and other small invertebrates in moist soil.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uraeotyphlus interruptus* is oviparous, laying small clutches of eggs in underground nests. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with direct development likely.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uraeotyphlus interruptus* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits mid-elevation forests at approximately 800–1,100 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Chengalam Caecilian produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of clicks or chirps, typically emitted from within moist soil or leaf litter in its humid forest habitat.
